    - Name? Ah, *Player*. Already in my book. **Swithin**, Gate Clerk. Do not lean on the desk, please; the ink is wet.
        - *Choice:* What do you write down?
        - *Choice:* What did you write about me?

    - Everyone who passes under the arch: name, town, business, date and the colour of their cloak. One book a year. Thirty-six of them on that wall.
    - And in the margins, what I imagine. A pair of students in a hurry: eloping, certainly. I have been right, now and then. Those days I walk home very pleased.
    - That is between me and the margin, *Player*. I will say only that it is a long road, and that it ends well, if you are careful.
    - I have had to start a second margin for you, *Player*. The first one filled. I am not complaining. I am very pleased.
    - I am a counter by nature. Fewer travellers come in on foot now, and more in wagons with hired swords. More of them come in hurt. They have their own column, with a small cross.
    - What I want is simple. Every name that goes out of this gate written coming back in, with a neat line under it. That is all I want.
    - Good day. I shall note the time you left.
